newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices supported amid crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices supported amid crude gains.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices were supported on Friday by overnight gains in crude values, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was offered at $98.5/$99.5 per tonne against a bid at $97.5. It was bid at $98.00 per tonne against an offer at $99.00 on Thursday.
Despite slightly increased interest, many traders said they took a wait-and-see attitude as there were no market-inspiring factors to stimulate trade.
Fewer exports from South Korea and overnight crude gains helped sentiment in the Singapore market, but some arbitrage cargoes arrriving in the Far East added pressure to prices, traders said.
"The market is quite directionless at the moment. Nothing is happening," said one trade.
On Friday, Taiwan's state oil company Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said it had awarded a 30,000-tonne cargo of high sulphur fuel oil loading between May 27-31 at under $100 per tonne on a fob basis.
CPC has also awarded a six-month term tender to buy low sulphur fuel oil at $28.60 per tonne premium to Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
Under the tender, CPC will take delivery of a 38,000-tonne cargo of low pour low sulphur fuel per month between June and November.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contrcat, only 40 lots were traded for June and July months, with June up 40 cents to $98 and July rising 20 cents to $97.8.
Sentiment remained bearish in the LSWR market over Indonesia's expected May allocation of 3.6 million Barrels.
As summer demand from Japan, a main LSWR importer, is expected to merge in late May, traders said prices were likely to move around current low levels.
